To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GADD34 protein targets the α isoform (PP1α) of protein phosphatase to the ER, and that this PP1α is required for dephosphorylating the α subunit (eIF- 2α) of eukaryote translation initiation factor 1.

the growth arrest and DNA-damage-inducible gene product GADD34 targets protein phosphatase-1 to the endoplasmatic reticulum (a subcellular compartment where protein folding occurs) and promotes dephosphorylating the α-subunit of the eukaryotic initiation factor-2, which is a protein that is involved in the initiation of translation of messenger RNA into protein.

the growth arrest and DNA-damage-inducible protein GADD34 promotes the dephosphory-lation of eIF-2a by targeting protein phosphatase-1α to the endoplasm-ic reticulum and that the N-terminal domain of GADD34 directs the localization of the GADD-34:PP1α complex to the ER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of protein translation in eukaryotes.
understanding the molecular basis for the regulation of protein synthesis in eukaryotic cells.
how cells respond to environmental and chemical stress, particularly the stress caused by protein misfolding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the growth arrest and DNA-damage inducible protein 34 (GADD34) targets protein phosphatase-1α (PP1α) to the endoplasmatic reticulum ( ER ) and promotes dephosphorylating of the α subunits of eukaryote translation initiation factor 1 (eIF2α).

the expression of GADD34 protein in cultured cells reversed the phosphorylation of the α-subunit of eIF-2 induced by okadaïc acid, but not that induced either by thapsigarin, an inhibitor of the endoplasmatic reticulum Ca-ATPase, or by tunicamycin.

the growth arrest and DNA-damage-inducible protein 34 (GADD34) associates with protein phosphates 1 (PP-1) and promotes dephosphoryation of eukarytic translation initiation factor 1 (eIF-1α) in the endoplamic reticulum (E.R.).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GADD34 is a PP1-binding protein that localizes at the ER and promotes dephosphorylating the α subunit eIF-2.
GADD34 is a PP1-binding protein that promotes PP1α localization to the ER and that this association is necessary and sufficient to promote eEF2α dephos-phorylation.
GADD34, a stress-induced protein, targets PP1α to the ER and promotes the dephosphoryation of the α subunits of eIF2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal region of GADD34 targets PP1α to the ER, where it can act on eIF2a.

GADD34 is an important regulator of protein synthesis in cells, and that it does so by assembling a PP1-dependent eIF-2alpha phosphatase that dephosphorylates eIF-2 alpha in response to a variety of ER stress signals.
GADD34 is a novel regulator of the eIF-2alpha protein phosphatase that is required for the recovery of protein synthesis following stress.
